about: Editor spec §42, problem_codes: the stable code of every problem the document profile reader raises (ProfileError), the same from the JavaScript and the Python libraries, and given as the Language Server Protocol diagnostic's code, so a problem's message and fix can be translated and looked up. A code is GN and three digits, numbered in groups by area: 1xx the header and tokens, 2xx the grammar and its values, 3xx the store, 4xx change sets, 5xx writing standard GQL. A code is never reused and never renumbered: a problem that goes keeps its code retired, and a new one takes the next free number in its group. message and fix are templates, each {name} standing for a part the problem fills in; section is the spec § they cite, or null. libraries says which library raises it: js, py or both. Every raise site passes its code as a literal; packages/graph-spec/test/problem-codes.test.mjs and python/graph_spec/tests/test_problem_codes.py hold each library to this table.

codes.message: the block names no graph
codes.fix: start it with '// graph: <name>' (§3)

codes.message: the graph name '{name}' is not one word
codes.fix: use letters, digits and underscores only — reader_choice, not reader-choice (§3)

codes.message: a comment must be on a line of its own: // also occurs inside identifiers, such as ni:/// hashes (§3)
codes.fix: put the comment on its own line

codes.message: cannot read '{text}'
codes.fix: a data block holds only nodes, relationships and simple values

codes.message: '{escape}' is not an escape GQL names
codes.fix: double the backslash to write a backslash: \{escape}

codes.message: expected '{expected}', found '{found}'
codes.fix: keep to the document profile (§3)

codes.message: expected a name, found '{found}'
codes.fix: keep to the document profile (§3)

codes.message: '{text}' is not a date
codes.fix: write DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD'

codes.message: '{text}' is not an instant
codes.fix: write DATETIME 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM'

codes.message: '{text}' has no offset
codes.fix: an instant carries its offset (§9, principle 11)

codes.message: '{text}' is not an instant: in UTC it falls outside years 1 to 9999
codes.fix: write DATETIME 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM' within years 1 to 9999

codes.message: '{token}' is not a value in the profile
codes.fix: use 'text', a number, TRUE, FALSE, DATE '…' or DATETIME '…' — no lists, no expressions

codes.message: id {written} is not text
codes.fix: write id: {quoted} — a node's id is always text (§3)

codes.message: SET would change {var}'s id, and a node's id never changes (§3)
codes.fix: write the right node, then link {var} to it or supersede it (§12)

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a data block ends after its INSERT and SET (§3)

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon, and graph {graph} has no relationship type called {written}
codes.fix: a relationship type is written with its colon: [:{type}]

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon, and graph {graph} has relationship types {types} and {last}, which differ only by case
codes.fix: write the one meant with its colon, such as [:{type}]

codes.message: this is a query block
codes.fix: queries ask questions of a graph; they are not data

codes.message: this is an excerpt
codes.fix: an excerpt illustrates part of a graph; it is not data

codes.message: MATCH must find a node by its id alone
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Label {id: '…'})

codes.message: MATCH finds no {labels} with id '{id}' in graph {graph}
codes.fix: the node must be written earlier — in this document or one loaded before it

codes.message: {var} is written twice
codes.fix: give each new node its own variable

codes.message: id '{id}' is already a node in graph {graph}
codes.fix: an id names one node (§10) — MATCH it to add to it, or supersede it (§12)

codes.message: {var} is used before it is written
codes.fix: write the node before any relationship that uses it — GQL binds a name only once its node is written (§3)

codes.message: no thing called {var} in graph {graph}
codes.fix: check the spelling — or write it here with its kind: ({var}:Kind {…})

codes.message: SET names {var}, which is no thing in graph {graph}
codes.fix: check the spelling — SET names a thing by its id

codes.message: a target is named by its id alone
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Kind {id: '…'}) — a thing by its name, a link by its two ends and its type

codes.message: a link is named by its type
codes.fix: write [r:TYPE] — a link by its two ends and its type

codes.message: a link is named by its two ends and its type alone
codes.fix: leave its values to a SET

codes.message: this names more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target (§24)

codes.message: {var} is not the one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target (§24)

codes.message: a DELETE needs the target it removes
codes.fix: write MATCH (v:Kind {id: '…'}) DELETE v

codes.message: DETACH is followed by DELETE
codes.fix: write DETACH DELETE v

codes.message: this removes more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target (§24)

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a DELETE ends after the one target it removes

codes.message: a link has no links to detach
codes.fix: write DELETE r

codes.message: a change is a DELETE or a SET
codes.fix: write DELETE or SET after the MATCH

codes.message: this changes more than one target
codes.fix: a DELETE or SET names exactly one target (§24)

codes.message: SET would change {var}'s id, and a node's id never changes (§3)
codes.fix: write the right node, then supersede it (§12)

codes.message: {key} is not a name a SET may give a value to
codes.fix: choose another name for the value

codes.message: unexpected '{token}'
codes.fix: a SET ends after its values

codes.message: the block names graph {named}, but the base gives it as graph {graph}
codes.fix: give it as graph {named} — a block is loaded into the graph its first line names (§3)

codes.message: id '{id}' is already a node
codes.fix: an id names one node (§10) — MATCH it to add to it, or supersede it (§12)

codes.message: cannot find where {var} is written
codes.fix: write it as (name:Kind {…})

codes.message: [{written}] has no colon
codes.fix: an engine is given only corrected text — read the block with its graph and load Store.corrected(block), or write it with its colon: [:{type}]
